title: The cartesian scalar pullback square agrees with the derived tensor pullback square
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes with small pro-etale sites in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For $Z=X,Y$ let $R_Z,S_Z$ be sheaves of commutative rings and $a_Z:R_Z\to S_Z$ ring maps. Specify $c_R:f^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X$ and $c_S:f^{-1}S_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}S_X$ with $a_Xc_R=c_Sf^{-1}a_Y$. Use module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact termwise scalar restriction $U_Z$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and K-flat scalar extension $T_Z=S_Z\otimes_{R_Z}^{\mathbf L}-$ with its representative-normalized adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Write $B_Z=U_Z(S_Z)$, placed in degree zero. Let $L_R,L_S$ be the exact cartesian-coefficient derived pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and let $b:U_XL_S\xrightarrow{\sim}L_RU_Y$ be the canonical action comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Let $\lambda:L_ST_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_XL_R$ be the localization of the balanced inverse-image/scalar comparison, with the normalization of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], transported along $c_R,c_S$.

There are natural isomorphisms
$$e_{Z,A}:U_ZT_ZA\xrightarrow{\sim}B_Z\otimes_{R_Z}^{\mathbf L}A,$$
whose map on any flat-term K-flat representative $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] is the localized ordinary balanced map sending $s\otimes p$ to $s\otimes p$. In particular, for every derived morphism $v:A\to A'$, $e_{Z,A'}U_ZT_Z(v)=(1\otimes v)e_{Z,A}$. Let $\mu_{B_Y,A}:L_R(B_Y\otimes^{\mathbf L}A)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_RB_Y\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_RA$ be the canonical derived tensor pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and let $\kappa:L_RB_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X$ be induced by $c_S$. For every $A\in D(R_Y)$ there is equality of the specified natural transformations
$$e_{X,L_RA}\,U_X(\lambda_A)\,b_{T_YA}^{-1}\,L_R(e_{Y,A}^{-1})=(\kappa\otimes1)\,\mu_{B_Y,A}.$$
On each flat-term K-flat representative $P$, both sides are the localization of the same ordinary cochain isomorphism; after the cartesian action identifications its degree-$i$ formula is $f^{-1}(s\otimes p)\mapsto c_S(f^{-1}s)\otimes f^{-1}p$ on local balanced generators, using sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These representative identifications are natural under cochain maps and quasi-isomorphisms between such representatives and determine the displayed equation on the whole derived category. No flatness of $a_Z$, boundedness, or projection-formula invertibility is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; agent scalar-restriction and K-flat localization normalization of its actual balanced comparison

proof.text: Write $Q$ for each derived localization. Fix the canonical total-tensor closed structure supplied by ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal and its simultaneous K-flat representative comparison supplied by site-derived-tensor-descent; these are the existing derived tensor of the statement. For any ring sheaf $R$, any $R$-module $B$ in degree zero, and any flat-term K-flat $P$, the canonical augmentation $\rho_{B,P}:QB\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP\to Q(B\otimes_RP)$ is invertible. Here is the normalization check, needed because $B$ need not be flat. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $r:V\to B[0]$. The one-sided tensor comparison gives $t_{B,P}:Q(B\otimes P)\cong QB\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP$, natural for $(r,1_P)$ and agreeing with the simultaneous comparison $t_{V,P}$. The augmentation theorem gives $\rho_{B,P}(Qr\otimes1)=Q(r\otimes1)\rho_{V,P}$ and $\rho_{V,P}=t_{V,P}^{-1}$. Naturality of $t$ therefore gives $t_{B,P}\rho_{B,P}(Qr\otimes1)=Qr\otimes1$. Cancel the isomorphism $Qr\otimes1$ to get $t_{B,P}\rho_{B,P}=1$, so $\rho_{B,P}=t_{B,P}^{-1}$. This identifies the one-sided model with the specified derived tensor, rather than an unspecified isomorphic tensor functor.

proof.text: For $Z=X,Y$, let $E_Z$ denote ordinary scalar extension and put $j_{Z,P}:U_ZE_ZP\cong B_Z\otimes_{R_Z}P$. Take the inverse, if necessary, of the ordinary extension/tensor comparison: its balanced formula in this direction is $s\otimes p\mapsto s\otimes p$. Applied degreewise this is a chain isomorphism, since both differentials send $s\otimes p$ to $s\otimes dp$. The normalized scalar adjunction computes $T_Z(QP)$ by $Q(E_ZP)$; exact scalar restriction computes $U_ZQ(E_ZP)$ termwise. Define on these representatives $e_{Z,QP}=\rho_{B_Z,P}^{-1}Q(j_{Z,P})$ using Step 1. The ordinary comparison and the one-sided comparison are natural for cochain maps; their chain naturality also respects chain homotopies, by applying the same equation to each degree of a homotopy. Thus they give a natural isomorphism on the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat complexes. Its two endpoint functors are the restrictions of $U_ZT_Z$ and $B_Z\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$, so they invert quasi-isomorphisms. The equivalence between the localization of these representatives and $D(R_Z)$, together with the natural-transformation localization property, extends it uniquely to $e_Z$. This proves $e_{Z,A'}U_ZT_Z(v)=(1\otimes v)e_{Z,A}$ for every derived arrow, including inverse denominators.

proof.text:
Denote the ordinary cartesian module inverse images by $I_R,I_S$. Their transported module presentations are supplied by geometric-module-construction with coefficient rings $f^{-1}R_Y,f^{-1}S_Y$, then transported along $c_R,c_S$, as in proetale-operations. They are exact and give $L_R,L_S$ termwise. If $P$ is flat-term K-flat on $Y$, preservation under ringed pullback makes $I_RP$ flat-term K-flat on $X$; apply the theorem with structural ring isomorphism $c_R$. Let $\chi_P:I_SE_YP\cong E_XI_RP$ be the ordinary scalar comparison, transported along $c_R,c_S$. Its localization is precisely the specified $\lambda_{QP}$ by scalar-comparison normalization. The ordinary action comparison $b^0:U_XI_S\cong I_RU_Y$ localizes to the specified $b$. Consequently, under the representative identifications of Step 2, the left side of the required equation at $QP$ is the localization of the ordinary chain map
$$d_P=j_{X,I_RP}\,U_X(\chi_P)\,(b^0_{E_YP})^{-1}\,I_R(j_{Y,P}^{-1}):I_R(B_Y\otimes P)\longrightarrow B_X\otimes I_RP.$$
The two $j$ maps retain their actual balanced normalization, and the action map changes only the ring action. Thus this expression is a computation of the specified composite, with no choice of a different scalar comparison.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); scalar-normalization representative theorem based on sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); agent cartesian action transport

proof.text:
Apply the derived/ordinary tensor pullback compatibility theorem to the two complexes $B_Y[0],P$. In its notation, $\alpha$ is invertible on every complex, because the cartesian-coefficient $I_R$ is exact and its derived functor is termwise. Step 1 identifies both $\rho_{B_Y,P}$ and $\rho_{I_RB_Y,I_RP}$ as isomorphisms, since $I_RP$ is flat-term K-flat by Step 3. Cancel these comparisons in the theorem's equation
$$Q(\delta)\alpha_{B_Y\otimes P}L_R(\rho_{B_Y,P})=\rho_{I_RB_Y,I_RP}(\alpha_{B_Y}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\alpha_P)\mu_{B_Y,QP}.$$
It follows that $\mu_{B_Y,QP}$ is computed, in these one-sided models, by the ordinary tensor comparison $\delta:I_R(B_Y\otimes P)\cong I_RB_Y\otimes I_RP$. The ordinary map $k:I_RB_Y\cong B_X$ induced by $c_S$ is $R_X$-linear because $a_Xc_R=c_Sf^{-1}a_Y$, and its termwise localization is the stated $\kappa$. Naturality of the one-sided tensor comparison for $(k,1)$ now identifies $(\kappa\otimes1)\mu_{B_Y,QP}$ with $Q((k\otimes1)\delta)$. No K-flatness of $B_Y$ or of $B_Y\otimes P$ has been asserted or used.

source.place: Tag 0FPH (lemma-tensor-pull-compatibility), with exact cartesian module inverse image; Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); agent cancellation of the one-sided comparisons

proof.text:
Compare the two ordinary maps from Steps 3 and 4. After the cartesian action identifications, both are induced by the bilinear pairing
$$(f^{-1}s,f^{-1}p)\longmapsto c_S(f^{-1}s)\otimes f^{-1}p.$$
For $d_P$, $j_Y^{-1}$ and $j_X$ retain the two tensor entries, $b^{-1}$ only restores the $S$-action, and $\chi$ is the inverse-image balancing comparison of scalar-normalization. For $(k\otimes1)\delta$, the normalized inverse-image tensor comparison first separates the two entries, then $k$ applies $c_S$ to the first. The coefficient compatibility makes these pairings balanced over the transported $R_Y$: the images of $(a_Y(r)s,p)$ and $(s,rp)$ agree by the tensor balancing relation and $a_Xc_R=c_Sf^{-1}a_Y$. Use the generalized-pairing formula of the inverse-image tensor comparison and the sheaf tensor universal property to conclude equality of the sheaf maps in each degree. This tests pairings from arbitrary test sheaves, and does not assume that every section of an inverse-image tensor is pure. The ring factor is in degree zero; both differentials are $1\otimes d_P$, so this is equality of the cochain maps $d_P=(k\otimes1)\delta$. Localizing proves the required equation at $QP$.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and preceding bilinear universal property; elementary equality of the normalized balanced maps

proof.text: Every object $A\in D(R_Y)$ is isomorphic to $QP$ for a flat-term K-flat resolution. Both displayed composites are already natural transformations: Step 2 supplies naturality of $e$, and $b,\lambda,\kappa,\mu$ are the specified natural comparisons. If $u:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, naturality expresses either component at $A$ as $G(u)$ followed by its component at $QP$ followed by $F(u)^{-1}$, where $F(A)=L_R(B_Y\otimes^{\mathbf L}A)$ and $G(A)=B_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_RA$. Equality at $QP$ therefore implies equality at $A$. The same naturality equations for cochain maps between representatives and their inverted quasi-isomorphisms give precisely the claimed representative compatibility. This proves equality of the specified transformations on the entire unbounded derived category.
